CanbusStats.Description: Round-trip time, retransmits, invalid frames and CPU load of the host and all MCUs on the CAN bus, aggregated in 2 second buckets. Records from app start, keeps up to 12 hours of history.
CanbusStats.NoDataYet: Connected, but no CAN bus statistics are available yet.
CanbusStats.Title: Canbus stats

Tooltips.BytesInvalid: Cumulative bytes received from the MCU that were discarded — either because they failed the CRC check (bit errors caused by electrical noise or a defective cable) or because they arrived with an unexpected sequence number. Any non-zero value warrants investigation.
Tooltips.BytesRead: Cumulative bytes received by the Klipper host from the MCU since the process started. Monotonically increasing.
Tooltips.BytesRetransmit: Cumulative bytes retransmitted to the MCU because an acknowledgement was not received before the RTO timer expired (host→MCU direction). Any increase indicates packet loss — check USB cable quality, CPU load, and MCU power supply.
Tooltips.BytesWrite: Cumulative bytes sent from the Klipper host to the MCU since the process started. Monotonically increasing.
Tooltips.HeaterPower: Heater power fraction 0–1 (2 s bucket average). Useful as context for CAN hiccups during prints.
Tooltips.McuAwake: Percentage of time the MCU spent outside its idle/sleep loop. Low values are normal. Sustained high values indicate the MCU is heavily loaded and may be unable to service all scheduled commands in time.
Tooltips.MemoryAvailable: Available memory of the host system in MiB (2 s bucket average).
Tooltips.RetransmitSeqs: The outgoing sequence number (send_seq) at the time of the most recent retransmit event. When this value changes, a retransmit just occurred. Use together with retransmit bytes to assess link reliability.
Tooltips.Rto: Retransmission timeout in milliseconds — the window before a frame is considered lost and retransmitted. Should stay near double the SRTT; if it grows, the link is having trouble.
Tooltips.RxErrors: Cumulative receive errors detected by the micro-controller CAN hardware. Increments on CRC errors, bit-stuffing errors, or framing errors on received frames.
Tooltips.Srtt: Smoothed round-trip time in milliseconds between host and MCU (host→MCU direction). Rising values indicate the host is getting slower at servicing the MCU, usually under CPU load.
Tooltips.SysLoad: Load average of the host system running Klipper (2 s bucket average).
Tooltips.TaskAvg: Average time in microseconds the MCU’s internal task scheduler takes to process a single command. Reported by the MCU firmware. Higher values reduce available headroom for real-time scheduling.
Tooltips.TaskStddev: Standard deviation of the MCU task processing time in microseconds. A high standard deviation indicates inconsistent scheduling latency which can cause timing jitter in stepper or heater control.
Tooltips.Temperature: Temperature reported by the sensor (2 s bucket average).
Tooltips.TxErrors: Cumulative transmit errors detected by the micro-controller CAN hardware. Increments when a transmitted frame is not acknowledged by any node on the bus. High values indicate missing bus termination, an open circuit, or a disconnected device. Note: rp2040/rp2350 MCUs always report this as 0.
Tooltips.TxRetries: Number of CAN frame transmit attempts that were retried due to bus contention (arbitration loss) or transmission errors. Only reported as non-zero by rp2040/rp2350 micro-controllers; always 0 on other MCU types.
